records.applicability: The pinned application graph contains braces only through development tooling. Current CI uses committed Tailwind content patterns and disables Karma watching. The inspected build path exposes brace expansion to repository-controlled configuration; no application-request or browser-runtime input path was identified. Development tooling may additionally process operator-supplied watch paths and filesystem-derived paths, so this exception accepts residual tooling denial-of-service risk. It does not establish that every possible invocation is unreachable or cover the publisher graph.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-03, the reviewed package and version investigation found no supported, compatible fixed route: braces 3.0.3 was the latest published release and inside the advisory's affected range, and the latest releases of its application-graph dependents (karma 6.4.4, micromatch 4.0.8 via fast-glob 3.3.3, and chokidar 3.6.0, still required by tailwindcss 3.4.19 and firebase-tools 15.32.1) still required braces 3.x; npm's suggested fix was a semver-major downgrade of karma. Without this exception every validate and certify run is blocked. The accepted residual risk is a denial of service in development and CI tooling. Remove this record in the same change that fixes or removes the affected braces in the application graph; from then on it matches nothing and the audit refuses it as stale. It expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-10-30 and is not extended automatically.

records.applicability: The pinned scanner bundles http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 through make-fetch-happen. The inspected npm 11.19.1 implementation constructs cache policies with shared: false, stores GET responses, and excludes Set-Cookie from its normal stored-header allowlist. The bulk advisory request uses POST and is not cache-served. These observations support a bounded exception for the advisory's shared-cache disclosure mechanism. They do not prove every invocation is credential-free or every audit input is independent of cache: the scanner preserves HOME, npm can read user/global configuration, and derived audit calculations use packuments. The scanner is tooling and does not ship in the application.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-03, the reviewed package and version investigation found no supported, compatible fixed route: http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 was the latest published release and inside the advisory's affected range, every make-fetch-happen release required ^4.1.1, and the distributed npm 11.19.1, 11.20.0, 11.21.0 and 12.2.0 tarballs each bundled the same 4.2.0, which the scanner lockfile and overrides cannot replace; npm's suggested fix was a downgrade to npm 6. Without this exception every validate and certify run is blocked. The accepted residual risk is disclosure or staleness confined to the scanner's own npm cache and configuration. Remove this record in the same change that fixes or removes the affected http-cache-semantics, such as a scanner pin to an npm release whose distributed tarball bundles a fixed copy; that change must also remove any other scanner exception that no longer matches. It expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-10-30 and is not extended automatically.
